```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

This guide opens invented discharges, defines a diagnosis cohort, builds a
survey design, estimates weighted summaries, and checks disclosure. All input
comes from `nis_example()`; it contains no real NIS records and results are
for learning only.

## Open annual data

`nis_open()` scans Parquet files lazily. Collect only a small summary when you
need to inspect records.

```{r open}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
nis |> dplyr::count(YEAR) |> dplyr::collect()
```

The counts here describe the synthetic fixture by year. See [Opening NIS
data](opening-data.html) for column selection and year coverage.

## Define a cohort

Flags check each diagnosis slot independently. Prefixes are analyst supplied;
easyNIS does not choose a clinical definition.

```{r cohort}
nis <- nis |> nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
nis |> dplyr::count(heart_failure) |> dplyr::collect()
```

The two rows show fixture records with and without a matching code. Review
positions and code-system assumptions before using a flag; see [Defining
cohorts](cohorts.html).

## Build a survey design

The cohort is declared inside `nis_design()`. This preserves sampled
hospital-year information when no discharges meet the cohort.

```{r design}
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS),
  annualize = TRUE
)
```

For a pooled design, `annualize = TRUE` divides discharge weights by the
number of valid years. The rule treats each included year as a whole year;
read [Survey design and weighting](survey-design.html) before choosing it for
a real analysis.

## Estimate weighted summaries

Use survey-aware summaries so standard errors account for strata and
hospitals.

```{r summaries}
srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS)
)
```

The estimated total and mean describe the fixture under its design fields,
not national estimates. The standard errors are design based; ordinary
row-level summaries would not represent this sampling design.

## Review disclosure

`nis_cell_counts()` reports unweighted discharges and distinct year-scoped
hospitals for each output cell.

```{r disclosure}
records <- dplyr::collect(nis)
cells <- nis_cell_counts(records, by = "heart_failure")
nis_suppress(cells, count_col = "n", hospital_col = "hospitals")
```

Suppressed rows either meet the configured small-cell threshold or represent
fewer than two hospitals. Review derived totals and follow the applicable HCUP
Data Use Agreement. See [Disclosure and suppression](disclosure.html).

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Filtering to the cohort before building the design drops sampled
>   hospital-years with no cohort records.
> - Treating the invented fixture's estimates as national results.
> - Sharing a masked table without reviewing totals and other derivable cells.

The exported `nis_new_study()` helper creates a new folder with a Quarto
project file and starter analysis. Add your data and revise the example code,
cohort, and study design for your question; the helper does not choose those
for you. See its function reference for details.
